summary: Runtime-backed throughput critique found that prepared useful work and recovery logic exist, but worker invocation/control-loop supply and live metrics wiring remain the dominant bottlenecks. A real claim race was safely recovered. A stale kernel attempt waited 8h22m from last signal to recovery start despite a 30-minute time gate, showing recovery semantics are not equivalent to continuous orchestration.

findings.finding: Useful READY work remained claimable while earlier high-priority lanes were stale/claimed; capacity must separate useful slots from actual worker supply.
Kernel original last signal 00:44 -> recovery STARTED 09:06; stale scanner is read-only and caller-driven, so the recovery event loop is not continuously driven.
Historical throughput snapshot is stale and the recovered deterministic progress compiler contract has no executable scripts/compile-progress-metrics.mjs yet.
Control Room canary proves fixture/loader semantics but explicitly does not prove a full live repository snapshot or allocator wiring.
A real create-if-absent normal-claim race was lost safely; the winning claim was preserved and this worker re-entered allocation and claimed the next READY opportunity.
Inspected GitHub automation compiles/publishes Agent Runtime on pushes/manual dispatch but does not close the swarm snapshot->stale scan->allocation->worker-supply loop.

remaining_boundary: No production scheduler, automatic ChatGPT/UI chat creation, global queue mutation, Current/Human Accepted/Served promotion, or serving change was authorized or performed.
